Could Coconut Coir be used instead of Peat Moss for gardening?

If so, what else needs to be done with the mix to make it fertile?

Peat moss is widely used with compost and vermiculite to produce potting mix. (It is much cheaper to make your own potting mix than purchase it.)

Unfortunately, Peat Moss is bad for the environment, and rather mined than farmed.

Does anybody know of a good, cheap, ideally organic source of Coconut Coir in the UK?
Down with Peat Moss! Up with Coconut Coir?!

I'm skeptical about coco coir. If you can afford it, it's a good product but I have doubts about it really being done sustainably at the industrial levels necessary to replace peat. I think bark based mixes are a more realistic path. I'll admit my knowledge on the subject is very limited though.

Also, my understanding is that there is processing necessary to remove salt from coco coir which is not done consistently by some manufacturers and can cause problems.

I'm also not a big fan of vermiculite. It can contain certain amounts of asbestos which don't have to be disclosed. I occasionally use it as a top dressing over small seeds but I never use it in mixes.

I use perlite and washed sand to improve wetting and drainage. Even when I buy pre-made potting mix, I add both. I've never seen a mix yet that wasn't improved by the addition of some sand.
